question: During the Mughal period, the Ain-i-Dahsala system was introduced by _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ain-i-Dahsala system** was introduced by **Akbar**, one of the greatest Mughal emperors, as a part of his revenue administration reforms.
 
• The system was developed by **Raja Todar Mal**, the Finance Minister of Akbar, to ensure a fair and systematic collection of land revenue.
 
• Under this system, land revenue was calculated based on the average produce and prices of crops over the last **10 years**. This helped create consistency and fairness in taxation. *Hence, Akbar introduced the Ain-i-Dahsala system.*
 
• **The system divided land into categories:** Polaj (cultivated yearly), Parauti (left fallow for 1-2 years), Chachar (left fallow for 3-4 years), and Banjar (left fallow for over 5 years).
 
• The system was widely regarded for its fairness and accuracy in assessing the agricultural productivity and tax potential of land. *Hence, the implementation of this system was a hallmark of Akbar's reign.*
 
• The Ain-i-Dahsala system also promoted a sense of trust between the farmers and the Mughal administration, as it removed arbitrary taxation. *Hence, the correct answer is Akbar.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akbar's Revenue Administration:**

 
 
• **Raja Todar Mal** played a crucial role in developing Akbar’s revenue system and introduced systematic measures for land taxation.
 
• Akbar implemented the **Zabt system**, under which land was surveyed and measured to assess its productivity and establish revenue rates.
 
• The **Ain-i-Dahsala system** was an important part of the Zabt system, ensuring revenue was collected based on a fair average of crop production and prices.
 
 
 
• **Categories of Land under the Ain-i-Dahsala System:**
 
 
• **Polaj:** Land cultivated annually.
 
• **Parauti:** Land left fallow for 1-2 years.
 
• **Chachar:** Land left fallow for 3-4 years.
 
• **Banjar:** Land left fallow for over 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Ain-i-Dahsala System:**
 
 
• It introduced a fair and predictable system of taxation, reducing the burden on farmers and encouraging agricultural productivity.
 
• The system promoted a sense of stability and trust between the Mughal administration and the agrarian community.
 
• It became a model for future revenue systems in India and influenced administrative practices during British rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Akbar’s Revenue System:**

 
 
• Akbar’s system relied on a detailed survey of land to ensure accurate assessment of taxes.
 
• **Standardization:** The system standardized revenue collection, removing regional variations and arbitrary practices.
 
 
 
• **Role of Raja Todar Mal:**
 
 
• He was a skilled administrator who introduced scientific methods for land measurement and revenue assessment.
 
• His innovations in revenue collection became a benchmark for future governance in India.
